p.title: Democratic roots in India
p.challenge: Put these 4 steps of India's democratic story in time order

panels.t: Rigveda: assemblies called sabha and samiti
6th c. BCE: ganas like the Vajji, capital Vaishali
10th c. CE: Uttaramerur, names drawn from a pot (kudavolai)
1950: Constitution gives every adult the vote

p.title: Is it a democracy?
p.challenge: Test a country: answer each question and see what every democracy must have

nodes.text: Free, fair, regular elections with real choice?
nodes.info: Rulers must be chosen by the people, and voters must have a real choice.

nodes.text: One adult, one vote, one value?
nodes.info: Every adult has one vote and each vote has equal value.

nodes.text: Rule of law and rights protected?
nodes.info: The law applies equally to everyone, including those in power; courts protect fundamental rights.

nodes.text: Not a democracy: no real elections
Not a democracy: votes are unequal
Not a democracy: no rule of law

nodes.info: It must also be accountable and transparent, for example through the RTI Act, 2005.

p.challenge: Arrange the 6 steps of an Indian election in order

nodes.info: The Election Commission of India (Article 324) conducts elections.

nodes.text: Polling day: vote on the EVM, check the VVPAT slip
nodes.info: Voting is secret; indelible ink stops anyone voting twice. NOTA lets you reject all candidates.

p.title: The Emergency (1975-77)
p.challenge: Drag the 5 events into time order, oldest on top

events.label: Indira Gandhi elected from Rae Bareli
events.info: On 12 June 1975 the Allahabad High Court declared this election void.

events.label: National Emergency proclaimed
events.info: 25 June 1975, by President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed under Article 352, on grounds of 'internal disturbance'.

events.label: Congress loses; Emergency withdrawn
events.info: Elections in March 1977; Emergency withdrawn on 21 March. Morarji Desai became the first non-Congress PM.

events.label: 44th Amendment adds safeguards
events.info: 'Internal disturbance' replaced by 'armed rebellion'; rights in Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended.

p.title: Government or governance?
p.challenge: Heavy rain has flooded the town. Sort each card: is it an institution (government) or the way the work gets done (governance)?

items.why: Parliament is an institution: the legislature that makes laws.
The Supreme Court is an institution: the judiciary.
A municipal corporation is a local government institution.
A State Legislative Assembly is an institution at the state level.

items.text: Planning how to clear flooded roads
items.why: Deciding and acting together is the process of governance.

items.text: Checking if garbage is collected daily
items.why: Checking whether the work was done is part of governance.

items.text: Asking residents before building a park
items.why: Letting people take part in decisions (participation) is good governance.
Keeping information open (transparency) is good governance.

p.title: Using the Right to Information
p.challenge: Someone's life is at risk and their family files an RTI. Follow the flow: how soon must the reply come?

nodes.text: A citizen asks a public authority for information
